@@ -1,4 +1,14 @@
 # QuestTogether client compatibility
 
+## Quest-starting item announcements
+
+Settings > QuestTogether > What to Announce > Quests > **Announce Quest-Starting Items** controls this event (on by default). It uses Blizzard's bag quest marker data, not Questie or QuestieDB. Only an explicit local loot message starts detection: the sender GUID must match the player, or a message without a GUID must match a localized self-loot format. A readable bag item with a quest ID and `isActive == false` confirms the same available starter shown by Blizzard's yellow exclamation mark. Ordinary quest items, already-active starters, bag moves and items present at login do not announce.
+
+Delayed bag/item data gets up to ten seconds to become readable, with at most sixteen pending item IDs and one bag scan per half-second. Duplicate observations of an item ID are suppressed for thirty seconds. Inaccessible or unsupported native data produces no speculative announcement. World departure, disable and profile replacement retire pending work. Browsing and detection never accept or select a quest.
+
+Events use normal announcement audience, chat, bubble and party-sharing policy. Sounds > **Party quest-starting items** controls the party cue. Typed item facts let receiving clients use their own cached localized item name; unavailable names retain the sender's item text. Older clients can still display the plain announcement. Offline fixtures cover detection, delayed data, locale formats, isolation and bounded work; live loot and two-client presentation need in-game confirmation.
+
+## Client families
+
 One source tree supports these current client families. Interface metadata permits loading; API capabilities still decide which adapter can run. PTR/beta builds in the same family use those adapters when their contracts match. This does not claim support for arbitrary historical/private-server clients.
 
@@ -43,4 +53,6 @@ Settings and owned windows use Blizzard's `MinimalCheckboxTemplate`, `ColorSwatc
 The minimap launcher uses an addon-owned button and tooltip, with a transparent 128×128 TGA generated from the scroll group in `logo.svg` by `scripts/build_minimap_icon.py`. Its guarded Minimap parent supplies position and scale; no scripts or addon fields are installed on Blizzard frames. Drag 
[... evidence excerpt shortened ...]
s for complete quest/objective text.
 
+PQL's **Filters** menu also provides **Quest area**, **Quest level**, and **Sort quests**. Combine **Current area** or a named area with **Quests I don't have** to find local catch-up quests; choose **Lowest level first** to prioritize lower-level quests. Area, level and sort choices are saved per profile, and Reset restores all areas/levels and the existing missing-first order. Level filters compare quest difficulty level with the local character's level, not the minimum acceptance level. Unknown levels have an explicit filter and sort after known levels in either direction.
+
+Area means the player's current zone (not the map being browsed). Compatible Forever QuestieDB metadata supplies a positive `zoneOrSort` area through its documented area-to-map mapping; negative quest categories are never treated as areas. Otherwise QT uses the guarded native next-waypoint map when available. These sources do not establish every objective location, and quests without readable coverage remain in **Unknown area**. Interior maps normalize to their containing zone when the map hierarchy is readable. Area names and quest levels are prepared with the existing deferred PQL snapshots; filtering, rendering and hovering do not scan the provider or request party data. Zone changes refresh the context while PQL is open. Filters apply to real party quest rows before chain grouping; contextual chain steps do not affect totals and retain their relationship order. Sorting preserves objective expansion. Live acceptance still needs a zone transition, combined missing/area filtering, level ordering, and controller selection of the new menu entries.
+
 Settings > Appearance & Accessibility provides 80–150% window scaling and reduced-motion scrolling/expansion. Scaling enlarges text and controls together; fitting the full window on a small display takes priority over the requested percentage. The Party Quest Log and welcome window save size and screen-relative position per profile. Restoring, reopening, changing display size, or changing UI scale clamps/fits registered QT windows to the current screen. Reset window layout (or `/qt resetlayout`) clears saved layouts and recenters windows. No layout state is stored on Blizzard frames. `Bindings.xml` exposes Toggle Party Quest Log in native Key Bindings with no default key. QT dialogs handle Escape through their existing dismissal actions; the libchev debug window is unchanged.

	local n = 0

	self.questStarterItems = nil
end
function QT:CHAT_MSG_LOOT(_, text, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, _, guid)

	local id = self.API.ReadQuestStarterLoot(text, guid)
	if not id then return end
	local now = self.API.GetTime()
	local state = self.questStarterItems
	if not state or state.profile ~= self.db.profile then
		state = { profile = self.db.profile, pending = {}, seen = {}, nextRead = now }
		self.questStarterItems = state
	end
	for item, expiry in pairs(state.seen) do if now >= expiry then state.seen[item] = nil end end
	if state.seen[id] or state.pending[id] or Count(state.pending) >= LIMIT or Count(state.seen) >= 64 then return end

	state.seen[id] = now + 30

function QT:UpdateQuestStarterItems()
	local state = self.questStarterItems
	if not state then return end
	if not self.isEnabled or self.isLoggingOut or self.isLeavingWorld or state.profile ~= self.db.profile then
		self:ResetQuestStarterItems()
		return
	end
	local now = self.API.GetTime()
	for id, expiry in pairs(state.pending) do if now >= expiry then state.pending[id] = nil end end
	for id, expiry in pairs(state.seen) do if now >= expiry then state.seen[id] = nil end end
	if not next(state.pending) or now < state.nextRead then return end
	state.nextRead = now + INTERVAL

		if state.pending[id] then
